content.title: Kid Rock Shows Off Photos of Army Attack Helicopters Over His House, Military Says It's Investigating
content.text: Kid Rock. Credit : Dia Dipasupil/Getty; Kid Rock/X NEED TO KNOW An investigation is underway after Kid Rock posted a video online that seemingly showed an Army helicopter flying low outside his Tennessee homeA spokesperson for the Army said that it had begun an administrative review "to assess the mission and verify compliance with regulations"Videos posted by the musician to X on Saturday show him applauding and saluting the helicopter as it hovers near his outdoor pool before flying off An investigation is underway after Kid Rock posted a video online that seemingly showed a U.S. Army Apache attack helicopter flying low outside the singer's home near Nashville. A spokesperson for the 101st Airborne Division, in Fort Campbell, Ky., told NBC News and local outlet WSMV that the two AH-64 Apache helicopters were following a training route in the Nashville area on Saturday, March 28 — and that their presence was "entirely coincidental" to the No Kings protests taking place that same day. The musician, 55, posted two videos to X on Saturday, showing him applauding and saluting a helicopter as it hovers near his outdoor pool before flying off. "This is a level of respect that s--- for brains Governor of California will never know," he captioned one post, referring to California Gov. Gavin Newsom. "God Bless America and all those who have made the ultimate sacrifice to defend her." "The 101st Airborne Division (Air Assault) and Fort Campbell maintain strict standards for aviation safety, professionalism, and adherence to established flight regulations," the spokesperson told WSMV in part. "We take all concerns regarding aircraft operations and their impact on the surrounding community seriously.” Maj. Montrell Russell, a spokesperson for the Army, also told Politico in a statement that the Army had begun an administrative review "to assess the mission and verify compliance with regulations and airspace requirements." "The Army is aware of a video circulating online that appears to show AH‑64 Apache helicopters operating in the vicinity of a private residence in the Nashville area," Russell said. "Army aviators must adhere to strict safety standards, professionalism, and established flight regulations." The Army will take "appropriate action" if it finds any violations took place, he added, per Politico. PEOPLE reached out to the Army for comment. Saturday also marked the third nationwide No Kings protest, during which millions of people took to the streets to march against President Donald Trump and his administration. The protests were organized by No Kings Coalition, a network of progressive groups opposed to the administration's agenda. Kid Rock introduces U.S. Vice President JD Vance to speak in front of members of the US Military on November 26, 2025 in Fort Campbell, Kentucky. Related Stories Kid Rock has been a vocal supporter of the Trump administration — and a critic of Newsom for the past several years. The singer recently headlined Turning Point USA’s All-American Halftime Show, the conservative group’s alternative programming to the 2026 Apple Music Super Bowl LX Halftime Show. The event was created after Puerto Rican reggaeton rapper Bad Bunny would be taking the stage as the Super Bowl Halftime Show performer, sparking backlash from conservatives, including Trump. Kid Rock has also been seen golfing with Trump and has visited the White House multiple times during Trump's two terms in office.
